title: Check yourself: Supplier's limits under threads and exceptions

questions.stem: Per this page, what can happen when two threads call get() on the compareAndSet memoizing Supplier for the first time together?

options.text: One of them waits until the other has stored its value
options.says: Nothing in the compareAndSet version blocks; the page says both threads may go ahead and compute.

options.text: Each may run the computation, and one of the results is kept
options.says: The page says racing threads may each call supplier.get(), and the losers' results are discarded.

options.text: Each may cache a result of its own, so later calls can differ
options.says: The page says compareAndSet stores only one result, so every caller sees the same cached value.

questions.stem: Per this page, what can `Callable<T>` do that `Supplier<T>` cannot?

options.text: Take an input argument as well as returning a value
options.says: The page calls both zero-argument interfaces that return a value of type T.

options.text: Return null as its value when it has nothing to give
options.says: The page says both can return null.

options.text: Throw a checked exception that its callers must handle
options.says: The page says call() declares throws Exception, while get() cannot throw checked exceptions.
